items.title: Critical NFS Server Vulnerability in Linux Kernel Disclosed
items.summary: A critical pre-authentication heap overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-99362) in the Linux kernel NFS server has been disclosed, with a CVSS score of 9.8. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to gain root access by sending a connection to tcp/2049, affecting systems using NFSv4.1 or 4.2 since Linux version 3.16. Fixes have been released in kernel versions 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, and 7.4-rc1, requiring users to upgrade and reboot their systems.
items.reason: The disclosure of a critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel NFS server with a CVSS score of 9.8 represents a significant security threat, as it allows unauthenticated attackers to gain root access. This has major implications for systems using NFSv4.1 or 4.2, making it a groundbreaking development in the field of cybersecurity.
items.author: zaihuapd

items.title: A Gene Informed Benchmark for BioScoring of Pathology Models
items.summary: The article introduces BioScore, a novel benchmark for evaluating how well pathology models capture cell identities, demonstrating its effectiveness through empirical scoring of multiple models.
items.reason: The article presents a novel benchmarking method, BioScore, that offers substantial technical depth and provides insights into the biological representation of pathology models, supported by empirical results and clear methodology.
items.author: Paul Vilars, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Maria Vakalopoulou et al.

blocks.title: Background
blocks.content: Traditional evaluations of pathology foundation models focus on their performance in tasks like classification and retrieval, which do not reveal the biological insights these models provide. This gap in understanding necessitates a new approach to benchmark these models based on their ability to accurately represent cell identities.

blocks.title: Solution
blocks.content: The authors introduce BioScore, a novel benchmark designed to assess how effectively an image encoder captures cell identities by comparing it to spatial transcriptomics data from the same tissue. BioScore employs a sparse autoencoder that divides the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which are then clustered into a predetermined number of groups. For each of the 52 defined cell identities based on marker genes, BioScore evaluates how closely each group aligns with the expression patterns of those identities across the tissue. This unsupervised training approach allows the model to represent cell identities based solely on image data. The authors tested eight pathology foundation models and three natural-image models, finding that all pathology models outperformed the natural-image models, with scores ranging from 0.299 to 0.371 compared to 0.214 to 0.232 for the latter. BioScore's ability to rank encoders without requiring labels and its detailed breakdown of identity capture provide valuable insights into model performance.

blocks.title: Takeaway
blocks.content: BioScore represents a significant advancement in benchmarking pathology models by focusing on their biological representation capabilities rather than just task performance. This method not only enhances the understanding of model efficacy but also facilitates the identification of specific cell identities captured by different encoders.

editorial.headline: Security Vulnerabilities Highlight Urgent Need for Tech Ecosystem Integrity
editorial.body:
Recent disclosures about critical vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel and the breaches affecting SAP and the US Air Force starkly illustrate the precarious state of cybersecurity across the tech landscape. These incidents serve as a wake-up call, underscoring how foundational systems and national security are intertwined with the integrity of our technology infrastructure. As attackers find new ways to exploit weaknesses, the stakes are higher than ever, especially for organizations that handle sensitive data or have national security implications.

While advancements in AI, such as Google's DeepCrossAttention, promise to enhance efficiency and capabilities, they also come with their own set of risks, particularly if security measures are not adequately addressed. The juxtaposition of rapid technological progress against the backdrop of security breaches raises pressing questions: Are we prioritizing speed and innovation over foundational security? As we advance into a future heavily reliant on technology, we must ensure that security is not an afterthought but a fundamental pillar of development.
